content: {"stories": [{"sourceBulletId": "B2", "organisation": "Australian Taxation Office (ATO)", "title": "Cutting SIT evidence effort by 92% with an approval-free harness", "situation": "Producing SIT and E2E test evidence by hand was taking roughly 3 hours for every scenario, and the volume across the squads made the planned test window impossible to hold.", "task": "I had to collapse the per-scenario evidence effort without buying new tooling and without waiting on a new approval cycle.", "action": "I designed an evidence-capture harness on the zero-new-approvals toolchain already licensed on the mainframe, then rolled it out squad by squad with a short enablement session for each.", "result": "Evidence effort fell from about 3 hours to about 15 minutes per scenario, a 92% reduction, and the test window became achievable again.", "metrics": {"Evidence effort per scenario": "3 hours to 15 minutes", "Reduction": "92%"}, "tags": ["test-automation", "delivery"]}, {"sourceBulletId": "B3", "organisation": "Australian Taxation Office (ATO)", "title": "Recovering a mathematically infeasible SIT window", "situation": "The SIT window demanded 75+ hours of manual evidence per team against only 64 available hours, so on the numbers alone the plan could not be delivered.", "task": "I had to turn an arithmetically impossible window into a plan the program could commit to, with a defensible decision point rather than optimism.", "action": "I ran a six-day tiered harness build, put a formal go/no-go gate at the end of it, and prepared a four-level contingency ladder so every outcome had a rehearsed response.", "result": "The 75-hour manual requirement was brought inside the 64 available hours and the window converted into an achievable, gated plan.", "metrics": {"Manual evidence required per team": "75 hours", "Hours available": "64"}, "tags": ["delivery-recovery", "planning"]}]}
